name: Jennu Kurumba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Upadhyaya, U. P. (1971). Coorg Kannada (Jenu Kuruba Dialect). Linguistic Survey of India Series 9. Poona: Deccan College Postgraduate and Research Institute. 8+88 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 3254.1.7 vol.9)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 1 Phonology (pp. 1-8: 1.1 inventory, 1.2 selected contrasts, 1.3 allophonic description, 1.4 clusters) never mentions stress, accent, prominence or intonation (a full-text search for stress/accent the full scanned text: only 'mistress' in the vocabulary). Only prosodic remark: 'A short vowel occurring in the final position is half-long phonetically' (p. 2). Data from Jenu Kurubas of Nanjarajapatna, Coorg, recorded 1967.

sources.citation: Shajan, Aiswaria G. (2021). Speech Forms of Kattunayaka in Wayanad: An Analytical Study. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, University of Kerala.
sources.note: Recent full-text linguistic thesis on Kattunayaka (= jenn1240 alt name) with seven chapters; open on Shodhganga but the bitstream server (port 8443) was could not be reached by automated download. Retry from another host or a browser; chapters 2-3 (57 KB / 117 KB) are the likely phonology chapters.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 langdoc list for jenn1240 (35 entries, downloaded as CSV) and Glottolog reference 557733 = Varghese, Bijumon (2015) The Tribes of Palakkad, Kerala: A Sociolinguistic Profile, SIL ESR 2015-028 (cited only for subclassification; covers Irula/Muduga/Attapady Kurumba etc., not Jenu Kurumba proper).
sources.note: Nothing; bibliographic listing only. Remaining Glottolog entries are ethnographic (Bird-David, Demmer, Misra, Fürer-Haimendorf, Menon, Fuchs, Luiz, Shashi, Bhanu, Naveh) and were not pursued.

sources.citation: Blair, F. et al. (2012). A Sociolinguistic Profile of Kurumba Dialects. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2012-015.
sources.note: Wordlist-based survey of Kurumba varieties including Jenu Kurumba; unlikely to state stress but would document which variety is which. sil.org blocked (not reachable by automated download) by automated download.

sources.citation: Zvelebil, Kamil V. (1980). Jēnu Kurumba: First Report on a Tribal Language of the Nilgiri Area. Proceedings of the Sixth Annual Meeting of the Berkeley Linguistics Society, 111-119. DOI 10.3765/bls.v6i0.2114
sources.note: Nothing. §2.1 'phonological features' (pp. 112-114) covers contrastive vowel centralization, nasalized vowels, v->b, *p->h->0, retained k- before front vowels, a nasalized bilabial fricative semivowel, *-d->-r-, palatalization of -d-/-dd-/-nn-; no mention of stress or accent. Data from Kadu Nayika (Kattu Nayaka) elephant mahouts at Teppakadu, Mudumalai, Nilgiris.

sources.citation: Nagaraju, S. and Lakshmipriya, K. K. (researchers; principal investigator Sujoy Sarkar; depositor Ashok Kumar G.). 2023-. Jenu Kuruba (ISO 639-3 xuj, Glottocode jenn1240): Scheme for Protection and Preservation of Endangered Languages (SPPEL) collection. Bhasha Sanchika digital repository, Central Institute of Indian Languages, Mysuru. 181 items (audio.wav elicitation/narrative/song, video.mp4). hdl:20.500.14705/11916.
Zvelebil, Kamil V. (1988). Jēnu Kuṟumba: Brief Report on a "Tribal" Language of the Nilgiri Area. Journal of the American Oriental Society 108(2): 297-301.
